newsitem.title: USA: Zenith obtains $400 mln in new financing.
newsitem.headline: Zenith obtains $400 mln in new financing.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp said Wednesday it obtained nearly $400 million in new financing commitments that will improve its financial flexibility and support its turnaround strategy.

It said in return for support from LG Electronics Inc, its majority shareholder, LG would get options to buy about 3.9 million Zenith shares at $0.01 per share. If exercised, LG's ownership would increase to 57.5 percent.
LG and its affiliate LG Semicon, currently own about 55 percent of Zenith's outstanding shares.

The new financing commitments include a $110 million asset-backed credit facility and a $200 million trade receivables securitization, provided by a banking group led by Citicorp and an $87 million leveraged lease transaction through Salomon Brothers.

The $110 million credit facility consists of two tranches -- a $45 million, three-year term loan and a $65 million revolving credit line and replaces Zenith's previous $110 million facility with GE Capital Corp.
The $200 million in trade receivables securitization is provided through a Citicorp commercial paper conduit with performance support from LG Electronics.

Under terms of the $87 million leveraged lease transaction, Zenith will lease back new and existing manufacturing equipment in its Melrose Park, Ill. plant. This will enable the company to further automate color picture tube manufacturing processses, expected to save more than $20 million annually, and begin producing 15- and 17-inch computer display tubes.

The lease agreement also includes machinery at Zenith's Reynosa and Juarez, Mexico facilities used to produce television cabinets and projection tubes for large rear-projection television sets. Zenith's payment obligations under the lease agreement will be fully guaranteed by LG.

As previously reported, Zenith has deferred filing its 1996 financial statements with the Securities and Exchange Commission and has scheduled its annual meeting, usually held in late April, for May 22. With the completion of the financing commitments, the marketer of television and video products will submit its final SEC filing.
